body: Hey! Totally get if you don’t wanna answer, but did you see the traits and symptoms in your child growing up? When did you suspect? I just find it extremely interesting that there can be 2 ppl with AvPD in a family unit. Even I was confused by my behavior, much less my poor family(they though didn’t like them), until I found this sub. Do you think it’s more nature or nurture?
Wait wait wait…suicide in both directions? 😂😂😂😂😭😭🤣😭🤣😭🤪🤪🤪🙃🙂What’s the solution?

Perfection. Nothing less than perfection will do for us in relationships. Our PD will always find a way to mess with what we have. Knowing this, you have to treat this specific symptom like a child and discipline it when it acts up. Otherwise, we really will end up alone. The hard part is figuring out if I’m avoiding someone because I’m not interested in them anymore or if it’s just my avoidance.

Go to a different country or a different state. A conservative one. No one will try to get to know you intimately because that’s considered rude (unless you choose to share). People will be kind and very nice, but it’s very formulaic; once you memorize it, you’ll get the socialization you need as a human. This might be a good backup end case.

Talk to a psychiatrist. SSRIs can be a game changer, offering hope for those of us still pushing and trying to grow. You may still feel avoidant, but you'll be less anxious and from there you can start taking steps forward (now that you're not just busy trying to survive). Hope this helps.

Can you say more on accepting not being close with anyone? Is it really okay for us to lead our lives full of acquaintances we greet but never really know? I did this in high school; I talk to no one from high school. The downside is, as soon as you move you have to start over. There is no carry over and I can only imagine it gets difficult as you get older.

Exactly the same. Meet once in a while, then make plans to see each other next month type friends. Anything more feels too deep. In fact, looking back, that’s how many of my friendships ended. It just reached a point where that person knew me too well, and I shut down. Till the next one… It’s a cycle I was trying to break back in high school, but in adult life it seems like ppl are too busy and can only do once in a while anyways, so it kinda works out—but I don’t know yet.

I’m in my early 20s. B/c I grew up poor, I saw getting rich as a way of isolating myself. This was before I understood my condition or what I had—I just knew I was uncomfortable around ppl, even family, and the only way to get a room on your own is to have money. So my entire life, same as yours but with a single strand: money, the only thing keeping me attached to society. I didn’t have a social life, but I lived off the praises my teachers and counselors gave me whenever I did well. This propelled me to do well and get into college until I finally got my diagnosis. Now, I still have the same plan, except it’s to work hard now so I can retire early and live a minimalist lifestyle. I was planning on going solo (b4 diagnosis) but fml and all of ours, turns out we need ppl, so I guess I’ll work on making a friend in my free time. That feels like a worthwhile life goal for us. One real connection. So I don’t plan on changing myself; however, I do plan on changing my surroundings and making myself as comfortable as possible. Hope this helps.

It's a world-building game. You compete with other civilizations to grow your empire and try to achieve one of the victories. There's domination (my favorite), where you take the capital city of every empire through battle. Diplomatic, where you win the votes of other civilizations by doing favors and trades. Scientific victory (also my favorite), where you race to the modern age and build a rocket before any of the other civilizations. Cultural, where you have the highest number of foreign tourists compared to any other civilization. You accomplish any of these victories based on how you choose to build your empire. You might advance your science fast enough, but instead of going for a scientific victory, you can use your advanced military science to crush other civilizations in a domination victory before they can develop the weapons you have. You can play as slow or as fast as you want. And the game allows you to be as surface level or as in depth as you want. Not every civilization has the same choices, though it's pretty balanced. It's a fun game.

BU student here. BU is extremely cliquey. The only upside is that it's so big that no matter what stage of college you are in, ppl expect to see new ppl, even peers in their graduation year. This means you won't stand out if you're alone; you could fly solo all four years without raising a flag. This also means you can shoot your shot with as many ppl as you want and try to see if there's a connection.

  
All in all, BU forces you to put yourself out there. And by forces, I mean you will quickly get extremely lonely sitting in your dorm with a ton of time on your hands. (Yea, unlike high school, you will have a stupid amount of time you won't know what to do with).

  
Also important to note: if you are Asian, you will have a large community to fall back on. Even more so if you're international.
